timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: AWS handles security, so we're safe, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: That's the shared responsibility trap. AWS secures the cloud, you secure what's in it.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Data, identity, access, and configuration. The part most breaches come from.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Least privilege. Roles for workloads, not long-lived keys lying around.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: VPCs with subnets, security groups as firewalls, network ACLs as filters. Segment everything.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: KMS for at rest, TLS for in transit. No exceptions.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Block public access, bucket policies, versioning. The classic leak vector.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: CloudTrail for API calls, CloudWatch for monitoring. Can't investigate what you don't log.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Multi-account with service control policies. Security baselines inherit everywhere.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Know what AWS does and what you must configure. That line is the whole game.
